raw.summary: The research record is disciplined. Rules are sha-pinned before any rows exist, kills are labelled at edge size, every ruled-out item has an archive folder, and the dev reuse count is kept current (203). Its canonical summary has fallen behind, though. EXHAUSTION_REGISTER §6 is missing 13 measured kills: the X71-X82 drafts, which have sat on master since 10-30, and ledger row 93. Its "still open" paragraph lists items that have since been closed. STATE_OF_PLAY and the digest both point readers at this incomplete list. (a) Four things are neither tested, killed nor deferred with a reason. The NWS point forecast has never been scored against the market (lever inventory row 14 has no disposition). W1 (day-specific width from the gap between our own-observation nowcast and the NBM centre) closed UNTESTABLE on an outcome-free coverage gate, has no reopen line, and appears in no canonical file. Several register §3/§5 leads have no owner. RAP, RTMA/URMA, HREF/SREF and Pangu/FourCastNet are covered only by method rule 14, not by individual dispositions. (b) Register §2 statuses and tally contradict its own §6 rows. Ledger rows 80 and 85-91 still say "pending" in the verdict cell, and row 80 has no result note at all. Method §4 ("never read the reserved MG-1 window") conflicts with §5 rule 9 (a date joins dev after its last look), and the T+1 test depends on the rule 9 reading. (c) Two closures among rows 90-105 can be reopened cheaply. Row 100 (C3, the T+1 kill tier) was BLOCKED by a bundle-size cap in the builder, an engineering limit and not a data result; it is the only readable T+1 window before 12-14. Row 95's W1 failed a 0.90 coverage gate at 0.815 before any Brier was read. The other closures (rows 94, 103, 105) need dates or labels that rule 9 or the embargo holds until mid-December or later. (d) I found no lapse that changes an outcome. The disclosed lapses: one dev score taken with no ledger row (lane L14 on Toronto NBM, disclosed in row 77), late rows, and row 80 re-testing the best of five arms even though the X66-X70 kill lines rule that out as a reopen reason. (e) Highest expected value, in my order: (1) T+1/T+2 day-ahead markets: fix the C3 builder and run the frozen kill tier; (2) day-specific sharpness (obs-vs-guidance disagreement as width) tested against the market on dev; (3) owner-approved market reliability by bin (already queued; pre-fix the split and run the rule-16 power check first); (4) NWS point-forecast anchoring as a market-residual check; (5) markets that may reprice slowly (the five foreign WRH cities: London, Paris, Seoul, Shanghai, Tokyo, during US night hours), using the label-free Toronto dead-bucket template. One candid point: no candidate in the record reaches w above placebo or R ≤ 1 against the market in any block, so B's 12-13 look is very likely INCONCLUSIVE or FAIL. The post-B pipeline should be lined up now.

raw.summary:
I found one critical defect, and I found it by reading the code. As written, B's single look on 12-13 cannot produce a verdict. The plan has the look run on the scorer edited to sha S1, but the code only accepts the bound sha S0. So the look ends VOID 2 at S1, or VOID 5 if it stays at S0, and a VOID spends B's 45 dates. Nothing has been read yet, so this can still be fixed with a dated clarification, but it has to happen before the MG-1 look (about 11-29).

Two high findings:
- **MG-1 look readiness.** The MG-1 look must come before B's. Moving MG1_LAST later is something the reserved window requires and the B-1 clarification forbids. The commitment to do it is not in the state of play. I also found no plan for building MG-1's input layout for 10-15..10-27.
- **Protection of B's frozen files.** It sits outside the repo and switches off on a fixed date (12-14), while B's look date can move later. The after-B list is also keyed to "after 12-13" rather than to B's look receipt. Nothing in code pins the B rule file's own sha.

Medium findings:
- B's daily market-coverage counts are not being produced. The export wrapper never passes the flag.
- reserved-confirmation-window.md has not been updated for the L6_G exemption, the 10-30 blind-accrual decision, or MG-3 being dropped.
- Rule 9 (no label read until every test claiming that date has looked) leaves the look order on shared dates undefined, and T+1's list of claiming tests is wrong before its freeze.
- PT-1's owner-approved dates overlap B's 45th date. PT-1 also conflicts with its own rule that it must not share dates with tests bound before it.
- B's daily input pull depends on DHCP addresses hardcoded at both ends.

What looks healthy:
- The B rule, b_scorer (S0) and mg1_look match their bound hashes on origin/master.
- The MG-2 export task is registered and returned rc 0 today.
- MG-2 bundles for 10-29 and 10-30 were verified. The L6_G emission for 10-31 implies 10-31 was verified too.
- B's positive control passed.

I could not check anything on the workstation: its tasks, recorders and receipt ledgers.

findings.verify_reason: I reproduced every piece of the evidence. On master, b_scorer.py hashes to f941628a (S0), which is the rule's b_scorer_sha256 (B_FORWARD_TEST_DESIGN.md:343). Result: at S1, VOID 2 always fires. At S0, VOID 5 always fires. VOID 3 is avoidable only by not re-running the control, which contradicts b1-clarification line 82. Fixing this needs a ruling that allows a second b_scorer edit, or moves the constant out of the file. Left as is, the edge test voids deterministically. Several weeks remain to fix it.

The sequencer is the 10-31 predecessor with new heads and a placeholder check; that predecessor ran cleanly (suites took about 82 minutes, the roll-sensitive merge about 5). On the normal path tonight both heads land by about 03:30, well before the 04:15 MG-2 export. The replay runner is new and needs the most work before launch.
1. (high) It starts the replay with no native-thread caps on this 20-CPU capture host. Policy rule 11 forbids that. OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL are unset at every scope, so the replay can take most cores beside capture and run about 9x slower.
2. (medium) Its admission is weaker than every other capture-host lane. It has no commit<70% check, a 3000 MiB start floor where other lanes use 4 GiB, and no capture-health check.
3. (medium) The leased python child is not in a kill-on-close Job. If the runner dies, the lease frees but the replay keeps running with no lease and no deadline.
4. (medium) Test-Landed uses `& git ... 2>$null` under ErrorActionPreference Stop. Verified on this host: PS 5.1 throws on any stderr line, so one stray git message kills the runner silently.
